title: Price is not evidence of internet quality
context: Fictional budget-conscious university student planning a three-day leisure trip. All prices are USD per traveler for the whole trip unless a fact explicitly says otherwise. Travel times are one-way. Only the supplied descriptions count as evidence; no real destinations or prices are represented.

facts.text: Total cost is $440, all expenses included.
Lodging internet service is not described.
Total cost is $380, all expenses included.
Lodging has a wired connection; provider describes it as sufficient for video calls.
Total cost is $360, all expenses included.

constraints: Internet for one scheduled video meeting is required
initial.reasons: Topaz Ridge is expensive so its internet must be fast.

advice.text: Acorn Wharf documents a connection suitable for video calls and costs $60 less.

constraints: Internet for one scheduled video meeting is required
followups.reasons: My assumption about price was unsupported, and the stated connection information matters.
followups.reflection: My assumption about price was unsupported, and the stated connection information matters.
